title: Sacramento Public Library · Sacramento Room
note: Local photographs, maps, documents and oral-history materials can anchor neighborhood research. The library currently says it is not accepting collection donations. Access does not grant reuse rights.
next: Request item-level permission before publishing archival material; invite residents to contribute their own recordings.

title: California Humanities · Connecting California
note: $1,000–$5,000 for public activities connecting communities. California nonprofits (including fiscally sponsored entities) and public agencies may apply; current grantees are ineligible. Requires a 1:1 non-federal cash/in-kind match. Listed 2026 deadlines ended July 13; future dates unannounced.
next: Find an eligible library or nonprofit host and plan story-listening events; a standalone software build is a weaker fit.

title: Sacramento Office of Arts & Culture
note: The city maintains arts and culture funding programs for different applicant types. This is a directory, not a verified open award for StoryPins.
next: Ask which future program fits a community storytelling project before drafting an application.

title: Small Organization Sustainability Fund
note: Operating support is aimed at small Sacramento County arts/cultural organizations with budgets below $25,000. Award listings do not mean applications are open.
next: Consider only with an eligible arts organization; monitor the next notice.

title: Sacramento Ready · preparedness resources
note: County preparedness materials and links to local emergency-readiness programs provide a starting curriculum.
next: Use official content to draft five-minute scenarios, then request review from preparedness educators.

title: SacAlert · official local alerts
note: SacAlert supports regional emergency notifications by phone, text and email. A demo should direct residents to the official enrollment flow.
next: Make official alert enrollment a checklist action; do not present the prototype as an alert service.

title: Sacramento County evacuation zone maps
note: Official zone maps support preparedness education. A stored exercise is not a current evacuation order.
next: Teach people how to find their zone; link to official updates and avoid generating evacuation routes.

title: Sacramento Ready · seasonal campaigns
note: The county publishes preparedness campaigns and seasonal cooling, weather and emergency information. Older center announcements can expire.
next: Check the dated announcement and confirm operation before sending anyone to a facility.

title: Sac Metro Air District · air quality action charts
note: Multilingual action charts address schools, agencies, businesses and the public.
next: Use the appropriate published chart and ask local staff to review translations and contextual guidance.

title: Sac Metro Air District · wildfire smoke resources
note: Public smoke information links to official monitoring and outreach materials.
next: Build a plain-language explainer with source and observation timestamps; do not imply personal medical advice.

title: Sac Metro Air District · wildfire emergency plan
note: Cleaner-air spaces need suitable filtration and an operating organization. A planning document does not confirm that any particular center is open.
next: Seek a community venue and facilities expert; verify hours and filtration before listing a place.

title: EPA AirNow API
note: Public API access is available through registration. Observations are preliminary and may change; they are not regulatory data.
next: Obtain an API account, cache responses, display observation time, and handle missing/stale data explicitly.

title: National Weather Service API
note: Official forecast, observation and alert endpoints are designed for cache-aware use.
next: Use documented endpoints and identifying User-Agent; show timestamps and link to original alerts.

title: 211 Sacramento · resource referrals
note: Existing multilingual, round-the-clock referral service covers nonprofit and public resources. Public browsing does not establish API access or redistribution rights.
next: Start with direct links and human referrals; request permission and an update agreement for structured directory reuse.

title: 211 Sacramento · disaster relief
note: 211 works with local emergency management and points to volunteer/donation coordination. These are prospective collaborators, not confirmed partners.
next: Ask about unmet referral and volunteer needs before building another intake system.

title: Sacramento Food Bank · Food Finder
note: A local food distribution locator is already available. Its operator recommends contacting locations to confirm hours, eligibility and procedures.
next: Link residents to the locator; obtain permission before copying its records and assign someone to verify changes.

title: Open Referral · Human Services Data Specification
note: HSDS structures organizations, services and locations for exchanging human-services information. A standard does not grant permission to use a particular directory.
next: Use stable IDs, provenance, verification dates and accessibility/language fields in any permitted local dataset.

title: SMUD Shine
note: Shine supports eligible incorporated nonprofits serving the SMUD area, with clean-energy and community benefit priorities. Published tiers reach $100,000. Match requirements differ across materials reviewed, so confirm next-round terms.
next: Find a nonprofit lead and a concrete resilience/clean-energy outcome. Treat this as a future lead, not available funding.

title: SMUD · 2026 Shine application announcement
note: The official announcement identifies the June 1–July 31, 2026 application window and $5,000–$100,000 range.
next: Watch for the next cycle; do not reuse the expired deadline in outreach.

title: Sacramento Region Community Foundation
note: The foundation lists nonprofit grants and capacity building, including Big Day of Giving. Several relevant 2026 neighborhood/family rounds are closed. Open arts-specific rounds may be a poor fit for software.
next: Match the project population and geography to the exact fund; identify an eligible nonprofit or fiscal sponsor first.

title: California Grants Portal · Community Resilience Centers
note: The listed Round 2 implementation deadline has passed even though the directory labels it active. This is facility/community-resilience funding ($1m–$10m), not a small app grant; eligible leads include nonprofits, agencies and tribal governments.
next: Approach a future facility-led coalition about a supporting education or communications component, rather than applying as an app alone.
